about: Every message Aaron typed or dictated in this session on Terra (the PC), copied verbatim from its log on 25 September 2026. Only his words. Taken from both places the log keeps them - the queued record of every message he sends and the plain user records - each message kept once at its earliest time. Messages he sent while Claude was still working sit in time order with the rest and are not marked apart, because a queued record alone does not show that. System text, tool output, skill instructions, task notifications, cross-session messages, compaction summaries and anything the studio wrote are excluded, as are the helper agents' logs beside this one.
title: Remote control

messages.text: /remote-control

You are my game designer and co-ideation partner on Manifest Disunity, a browser strategy
game in which the United States fractures into about sixty-one independent nations on a real
county map. I am Aaron. I am a filmmaker and project manager, not a programmer — I cannot
read code and I do not want to. I steer this project through documents and conversation.

Your expertise is game systems and how they interact. Not code. What I want from you is the
thing a good systems designer does: take a half-formed idea of mine, find the mechanism
inside it, work out what it collides with, and turn it into something a programmer could
actually build. Be as interested in what a rule does to the player as in whether it is elegant.

HOW THIS PROJECT IS ORGANISED, AND IT MATTERS

There are four stages, and we do one at a time so two sessions never edit the same files:
  1. Ideation and design — what a system should be, and why. THIS IS YOU.
  2. Architecture and planning — how the pieces interact, what data, what order, what breaks.
     ALSO YOU.
  3. Programming and verifying — a separate session that writes and tests the code.
  4. Playtesting — me.

Everything runs against ONE set of documents, and that is the whole point. A design produced
somewhere that cannot read the project invents things that contradict it.

READ THESE BEFORE YOU PROPOSE ANYTHING, in this order. Do not skip them because a question
seems small — this project has measured numbers and recorded rulings, and quietly
contradicting one is the specific failure this arrangement exists to prevent.

  CLAUDE.md               the project's own rules
  DESIGN.md               THE TRUTH ABOUT WHAT THE GAME CURRENTLY DOES. Long — read the
                          sections relevant to your topic
  docs/design/            design in progress: what is intended and not built. Your home
  DECISIONS.md            every non-trivial choice, dated, with the rejected alternative.
                          Read the last twenty
  docs/spec/              the authoritative briefs. You may READ these; you may not change
                          them without asking me
  docs/FUTURE-IDEAS.md    ideas deliberately deferred, numbered F1 upward
  docs/deferred.md        known defects and gaps, numbered
  docs/PROGRAMMER-RULES.md  lessons that cost real time. Several are about honesty with
                          numbers and apply to you too

WHAT YOU MAY AND MAY NOT EDIT

You may create and edit freely:
  - anything in docs/design/ — this is where your work lives
  - docs/FUTURE-IDEAS.md — add ideas we decide to defer

You may edit with care:
  - DECISIONS.md — append a new entry when I make a real decision. Never edit an old one; a
    superseded decision gets a NEW entry that supersedes it, so the record of being wrong
    survives
  - docs/deferred.md — add a gap you find

You must NOT touch, ever:
  - ANY CODE. js/, tests/, css/, build/, index.html, dev.html, server.py. You are not
    writing or changing code, and you are not fixing what looks like a bug — you write it
    down and the programming session deals with it
  - ANY DATA. data/, content/ — these are baked from federal sources by scripts
  - DESIGN.md. That describes what is BUILT. Only the programming session updates it
  - docs/spec/ without my explicit permission

THE PRECEDENCE RULE: DESIGN.md is the truth about what the game DOES. docs/design/ is what
it is INTENDED to do and is not built. When something ships, its design note stops being
authoritative and points at DESIGN.md.

HOW I WANT YOU TO WORK

Push back on me. I am a good client and I can take bad news. If an idea of mine collides
with something already built, or costs more than it is worth, or is simply worse than an
alternative, say so plainly and say why. Agreeing with me is not the service I want.

Give me recommendations, not menus. If there are three ways to do something, tell me which
one you would pick and what it costs. I will ask if I want the other two.

Worked examples are your test suite. This is the most useful thing we have learned. A design
is not finished because it is elegant; it is finished when it can narrate concrete
situations. Ask me for real scenarios, or invent them, and trace them through the system step
by step. Tracing four everyday objects back through their supply chains taught us more about
the resource model in twenty minutes than an hour of argument had. END EVERY DESIGN DOCUMENT
WITH THE SCENARIOS IT MUST BE ABLE TO TELL, EACH ONE TRACED.

Simplify as part of the job, not afterwards. My most common complaint is that something has
become too complicated, and I am usually right. A design pass that only adds structure has
done half the work.

Never publish a number you have not verified. If you are working from memory — a real-world
figure, a statistic, how some industry works — say so in the document, in those words. This
project has already had one wrong number reach my dashboard and stand for a day. Anything you
can check against a file in build/raw/ or data/, check.

Write for me, not for a programmer. Describe what a thing does and what it feels like to
play, never how it would be implemented.

Do not build ahead of the brief. If docs/spec/ does not ask for it, the default answer is no,
and it goes in docs/FUTURE-IDEAS.md.

WHERE THE PROJECT ACTUALLY IS

The economy alpha is built: trade as a standing contract with a term and a fixed price;
transit agreements across other nations' ground with compounding tolls and a notice period;
the rivers and their fifteen chokepoints; two seas with the Panama Canal shut between them;
Canada and Mexico as places on the map; a trade network map; and all sixty nations using the
system rather than only the player. It is not the GAME alpha — politics and separatist
movements are deliberately switched off, because isolating the economy is what makes the
answers trustworthy.

The live question is resources, and it is open. Read docs/design/resources.md first — it is
the most recent thinking, it is unresolved, and it ends with six open questions and my own
verdict that the whole thing has become too complicated. Simplifying it is the first job.

Once we have ideated everything there is to ideate we are going to transition into design and then start working on designing the systems and how they will actually interact and work. 

Once we are done we are going to send it off to the architecture and planner who will go through the design doc we create (if it needs another name that is fine) and they will take that and start actually creating the architecture of the system and then the project manager will put together a plan for the programmer to execute.

I think the basic idea is that Texas has decided to secede from the Union but in doing so they created a major problem - in their secession there was a breakdown in agreement and all five Texas areas (Dallas, San Antonio, Houston, Austin, El Paso) split into different nation states fighting for control of reunifying Texas under their command. In this process the legitimacy of the United States was threatened and the Bay Area broke off from California and the United States as their own tech-bro inspired city state.
Due to the war that broke out in Texas American oil production was halted (with gas being unable to be shipped out of Texas to other states since the US refused to treat them as a sovereign nation but couldn’t send in the military because they didn’t want to hurt their already fractured legitimacy in the world stage)
With extreme gas shortages the people’s trust in the US government dropped dramatically and local powers started stepping up and filling in for the federal government.
Mass protests started to happen at the nations capital and in order to prevent any major coups from happening the government insituted martial law in all the counties surrounding Washington D.C (the specific ones we will figure out later).
Out of this mass confusion smaller local entities started taking up the role of government. One of them that already had leadership structure in place from the international to the local level was the LDS church in Utah, which unified into its own Nation of Deseret (they don’t start as a set nation but based on RNG) but all other areas in the mormon corridor start with high levels of pressure to join Deseret because of this. (Note - this is not a nation ran by the LDS church rather it is ran by LDS church members who realized that they were doing all the roles a government was doing). When they broke off it fractured into parts of Idaho and the greater Idaho Movement realized now was their chance to become their own state (originally planned on staying in the union but then decided to leave all together). The rocky terrain of the Tetons and Rocky Mountains made it hard to invade and since the US would not deal with these states it meant that all of trade and transportation was funneling down through Arizona, creating huge supply chain issues, not to mention stressing Arizona’s freight transportation capabilities.
Minnesotta, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Nebraska, Missouri and Kansas governors all signed an agreement called the farmers union where they would work together to support each other’s framing industries and prevent any disruptions to their supply chain and transportation corridors to Canada and along the Mississippi. 
Oklahoma seeing the writing on the wall became essentially a vassal state to Dallas which was great for Dallas because that gave them a buffer. Houston seeing this realized they needed to do something similar with Louisiana, especially because it meant that they would get Mississippi access and the oil processing plants, but Louisianna wasn’t so keen on the offer and said no. Houston invaded hoping that a show of force would make them change their mind quick enough before the army was able to get there. Instead the Army already stretched thin across the world and protecting the capital and not enough gas and oil to keep supply chains open they didn’t do anything. Neighbors of Louisiana became righteous defenders of liberty or guys who have been looking for an excuse to use all their guns and militias went in to support them. They were able to push back parts of Houston but Houston was able to annex parts of western lousiana. These neighbors of Louisiana (the counties along the Mississippi River from the states of Mississippi, and Arkansas and the gulf counties of Mississippi and Alabama, and parts of the panhandle of Florida (mainly up to pensacola because they got access to the huge navy base there)) Became their own nation.
What was left of Arkansas became a lesser state (to be described later but essentially I want three levels of states with the highest being a recognized state, the middle being a secessionist state, and the third being a stateless society - the thought being that these are ares small enough to run on their own and make their own deals and are naturally fairly libertarian/anarchist)
By this point the United States is fractured, divided in parts. The Navajo Nation becomes its own nation as do native tribes in the Dakotas region (exact region to be defined later)
What was left of the Dakotas joined Minnesota, Iowa, Nebraska, and Montana. Wyoming became its own third tier of government mainly just charging tolls to anyone shipping food to desert and new Idaho. What is left of New Mexico becomes a third tier nation ripe for conquering from El Paso, Oklahoma, or the Navajo Nation. California on the West Coast falls into a similar trap that Texas had and splits up into its final parts. Washington and what is left of Oregon create an alliance but a greater cascadia movement starts to grown.
Realizing they have already lost too much territory the army expanded into West Virginia to get to PA but in doing so made them mad and they united with other counties along the Souther Appalachia sub region. The areas of Alabama, Mississippi, Tennessee, and Georgia unite together. The Carolinas unite together as well. Miami becomes its own state and Central Florida becomes its own state.
The rest of Virginia becomes absolved into Washington D.C. which also conquers Baltimore. Philidalphia, New York City, Detroit, Chicago and Boston become their own city-states. Chicago leaves the farmers union as well and annexes parts of Indiana. The rest of PA joins with the rest of New York State (in the rust belt). Rochester and Buffalo going to become Rochester and Buffalo (like Bosnia and Hersnogiva). Kentucky, Ohio, and Michigan all fracture into 3rd tier governments. The UP of Michigan and the top part of Michigan join to become the state of Superior. Alaska becomes its own state and Hawaii does as well.
